thread:
incident-bot: PAGING — High-severity incident detected for customer Hydrangea (tenant H-522). Region: us-east-1. Symptoms: 95th p99 latency spike for inference RPCs, elevated 5xx from dedicated pool, ~30% request errors for enterprise routes.

pagerduty-bot: Triggered by metric threshold breach: redwood.inference.tenants.H-522.p99 > 1200ms for 3m. Incident created: INC-20260315-42.

maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it — paging eng-sre and platform. @alex @jin can you join? I'll start customer comms.

alex (eng-platform): here. Seeing repeated connection resets from the us-east dedicated pool to GPU nodes. Control plane reports high KV cache miss rate and node-level OOMs on a subset of hosts.

jin (eng-sre): joining. Pulling logs now. Do we have a recent deploy to that pool?

ops-telemetry-bot: Recent deploy: model-serving:release-2026.03.14 pushed to us-east-1 pool at 03:05 UTC. Error spike starts ~03:12 UTC.

maya (oncall): timeline looks aligned with deploy. But we also have a customer request surge (Hydrangea) — lia reported a big job earlier. @lia, details?

lia (solutions): customer ran a heavy batch eval at 02:58 UTC, estimated peak QPS ~3x baseline for H-522. They said it was a rolling eval across many endpoints.

carter (netops): network metrics look stable at infra level; no obvious packet loss. However EC2 host memory pressure is high on several nodes in dedicated pool dpool-us-east-H-522.

alex (eng-platform): plan: temp isolate tenant from the affected dedicated pool and shift traffic to warm standby in us-west-2 while we drain nodes and rollback suspect release. Recommend staged traffic shift: 10% canary -> 50% -> 100%. Need to lower DNS TTL for Hydrangea endpoints first to accelerate cutover.

maya (oncall): agree. I'll coordinate with customer. Sara — can Hydrangea accept short 1–2 minute request loss during shift? Also can they reduce client-side retries?

sara (Hydrangea-SRE): We're online. We can accept a short interrupted window, prefer the canary approach. We'll lower our own client timeout to shorten tail. Also we can temporarily route traffic from our side if needed.

jin (eng-sre): technical checklist for failover:
- create snapshot of current routing rules
- disable routing to affected nodes
- warm us-west-2 dedicated pool (dpool-us-west-H-522) if not already warmed
- set DNS TTL to 30s for hydrangea.redwood.example.com
- shift 10% traffic using rdctl route-shift (see command)
- monitor 5xx and p99 for 10 minutes, escalate on >1.5x error or p99 > 800ms

alex (eng-platform): warming status: dpool-us-west-H-522 shows idle capacity 120% of baseline (we had warm capacity reserved after the customer's Dedicated plan). Good to go.

carter (netops): I'll prepare the DNS change. Note: authoritative provider (FastDNS) needs API keys. Have them ready.

maya (oncall): executing pre-failover steps now. Backing up routing config.

--- 03:22 UTC ---

maya (oncall): rdctl snapshot routes --tenant H-522 --out /tmp/H-522.routes.snap

ops-telemetry-bot: Snapshot complete. Size: 6.1KB.

alex (eng-platform): pausing new deploys to the cluster and enabling rollback safety gates.

carter (netops): making DNS change: setting hydrangea.redwood.example.com TTL 30s.

carter (netops): API call to FastDNS: PATCH record hydrangea.redwood.example.com TTL=30 — 200 OK. Propagation should start now.

maya (oncall): Starting traffic shift canary -> 10% to us-west-2. Command: 

```
rdctl route-shift --tenant H-522 --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --percent 10 --policy canary --reason "inc-INC-20260315-42"
```

alex (eng-platform): executed. Router logs: shift ticket created id=rs-5821.

ops-telemetry-bot: Canary metrics (2m window): error-rate down from 30% -> 27% on overall; canary segment shows 5xx=0.8%, p99=410ms. Baseline us-east still degraded p99=1150ms.

jin (eng-sre): good signal. Proceed to 50% if stable for 10m.

maya (oncall): customer notified: "We are shifting a small portion of your traffic to warm failover to stabilize. Expect brief retries. We're monitoring closely." Sara acknowledged. :thumbsup:

--- 03:40 UTC ---

alex (eng-platform): shifting to 50%. running: 

```
rdctl route-shift --tenant H-522 --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --percent 50 --policy gradual
```

ops-telemetry-bot: Shift in progress.

ops-telemetry-bot: After shift: overall error-rate reduced to 6.2%, p99 overall 520ms. us-west segment stable (p99=420ms, 5xx=0.9%). us-east still hitting node failures.

jin (eng-sre): we're seeing crash loops on model-worker processes on 3 hosts. Collecting core dumps and starting controlled drain of those hosts from dpool-us-east-H-522.

alex (eng-platform): starting rollback of model-serving:release-2026.03.14 on the pool. This should free memory pressure.

carter (netops): DNS TTL is low; per FastDNS analytics, most clients now respect new TTL, helps cutover speed.

--- 03:55 UTC ---

jin (eng-sre): rollback successful on drained hosts, GC pressure reduced, core dumps uploaded to s3://incidents/INC-20260315-42/cores.

ops-telemetry-bot: Post-rollback metrics: us-east p99 dropping to 460ms, 5xx ~1.1%.

maya (oncall): decision time: do we continue shifting back to us-east or keep customer on us-west permanently? Need customer preference and SLA impact.

sara (Hydrangea-SRE): We prefer minimal DNS churn. If us-east is stable and passes 30m of normal load, we can move back tomorrow EOD. For now, keep majority on us-west to stabilize.

alex (eng-platform): switching routing to keep 85% on us-west, 15% on us-east for resiliency and to let us-east finish healing.

```
rdctl route-shift --tenant H-522 --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --percent 85 --policy manual
```

ops-telemetry-bot: Change applied. Current split: us-west 85% / us-east 15%. Overall p99=380ms, 5xx=0.6%.

maya (oncall): customer update sent: summary of actions and ETA for follow-up. 

sara (Hydrangea-SRE): Thanks — appreciate the quick response. We'll keep monitoring from our side and will pause large batch jobs for 6 hours.

--- 04:20 UTC ---

jin (eng-sre): creating incident runbook snippet for postmortem: suspected cause = memory regression in release-2026.03.14 combined with unusually high eval QPS from customer leading to OOMs. Action items: revert change permanently until root cause fixed, increase canary windows for future releases, strengthen per-tenant circuit breakers.

alex (eng-platform): provisioning note: reserve larger warm pool for H-522 during known heavy eval windows (lia to coordinate scheduling with customer).

maya (oncall): handoff: I'm handing incident to Night-Shift SRE at 08:00 UTC. Leaving follow-up tasks assigned.

maya (oncall): final incident update: majority traffic shifted to us-west warm pool, us-east drained and stable, customer on standby and paused heavy jobs, rollback performed. Closing paging for now, monitoring in watch channel.

ops-telemetry-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring): INC-20260315-42 — status: mitigated.

--- Post-incident notes (added to thread) ---

alex (eng-platform): tagging follow-ups: ACTION-389: permanent rollback and bisect of release-2026.03.14; ACTION-390: add tenant-aware memory quotas; ACTION-391: update deployment runbook to require per-tenant dry-run for heavy-change windows.

lia (solutions): I'll coordinate with Hydrangea for a scheduled maintenance window next week to test full failover practice.

maya (oncall): good job team. Closing thread. :tada:
